clue.text: Military establishment given natural backing after hostilities

parts.note: a post is a station where troops are based

indicators.note: backing means going in the opposite direction, so the word for natural is read from its end

parts.note: raw means in its natural, unprocessed state

explanation.surface: An army base gets a natural defence once the fighting is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Hostilities looks like part of the military picture, but 'after hostilities' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something postwar belongs to the period following a war, once hostilities have ended.

clue.text: Roman Catholic priest initially disposed to protect lives?

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word priest

parts.note: first letter

indicators.note: to protect is to shield, so one part wraps around the other

parts.note: apt means inclined or disposed
is means lives or exists

explanation.surface: A Catholic cleric inclined to safeguard life.
explanation.walkthrough: Lives is the verb, meaning exists, not the plural of life. Papist is an old and usually hostile word for a Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: Papist is a derogatory term for a Roman Catholic, from their allegiance to the Pope.

clue.text: Like Sagittarius, the Archer, viewed in South America? Right

indicators.note: something viewed in a place is seen inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: standard abbreviation
William Tell, the legendary Swiss bowman
R for right

explanation.surface: The constellation of the Archer, as seen from South America, and that is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archer is the name of Sagittarius too, but here it is the archer William Tell, inside SA, then R.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar means relating to stars, and Sagittarius is a constellation of stars.

clue.text: Look out for game in this store

parts.note: ware is an old word for beware, as in 'ware wire'
house is the old name for bingo

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out for wildlife in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Game suggests hunted animals; it is the British name house, an older term for bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: A warehouse is a large building where goods are kept before sale or distribution.

clue.text: Disturbing leak — Tripoli provides opportunist government

indicators.note: disturbing means throwing into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A worrying leak from the Libyan capital points to a cynical regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Realpolitik is politics driven by practical advantage rather than ideals or morality.

clue.text: Agricultural fellow detailed to improve crops primarily

indicators.note: de-tailed means having its tail cut off, so the final letter goes

parts.note: George stands for any man or chap

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of each of the words just before it

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A farmhand is assigned the task of boosting the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: GEORGE loses its last letter to leave GEORG, then IC completes GEORGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgic means relating to farming, from Virgil's Georgics, his poems on rural husbandry.

clue.text: Information that's withheld from a supernatural spirit

indicators.note: withheld from means kept back from, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: a genie is a spirit of Arabian legend
i.e. stands for id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Secret knowledge kept from a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: IE is removed from GENIE to leave GEN, British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Gen is informal British slang for the facts or information about something.

clue.text: A sort of appeal thus raised in the old town

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
it means sex appeal
so means thus

explanation.surface: A kind of plea is therefore made in the ancient settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: A, IT and SO run upward to give OSTIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the ancient port city at the mouth of the Tiber serving Rome.

clue.text: Nanny, possibly, carrying a French baby's first vessel

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the goat wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a nanny is a female goat
un is French for a

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word baby

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A nursemaid holds a French child's first boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Nanny suggests a nurse, but it is a goat; G-OAT holds UN and B.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunboat is a small armed vessel, used for patrolling coasts and rivers.

clue.text: Mary was just the opposite!

parts.note: surface reading: someone called Mary behaved in the reverse way to expected
setter's reading: the nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite ...', where the word that ends the line also means opposite

explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the English nursery rhyme beginning 'Mary, Mary, quite ...', which asks how her garden grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary means opposite in nature or direction, and also wilfully perverse, like Mary in the rhyme.

clue.text: Determine beforehand that the redcoats are in trouble

parts.words: Determine beforehand that the redcoats are in trouble
parts.note: surface reading: someone foretelling that British soldiers will meet disaster
setter's reading: to decree or appoint an outcome in advance, as fate does

explanation.surface: A prophet decrees that the British army is heading for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as PRE (beforehand) and ORDAIN (determine); the rest of the clue is a picture of fate deciding a battle in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To preordain is to decree or settle something ahead of time, as destiny is said to.

clue.text: Projection of deal, possibly

parts.note: surface reading: a forecast of how a business agreement might turn out
setter's reading: deal is pine or fir timber, and the projection is a shaped tongue of wood

explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a carpenter's word for softwood planks; the projection is the one that fits into a mortise joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the protruding end of a piece of timber, cut to slot into a matching hole in another.

clue.text: Slender girl in the Strand, returning in silence

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other, here enclosed by the hush

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way it went, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: a ply is one strand of yarn or rope

explanation.surface: A slim young woman walks quietly back along the Strand in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand looks like the London street, but here it is just a strand of thread or yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: A sylph is an airy spirit, and by extension a slim, graceful young woman.

clue.text: Display a severe hair style

parts.note: pomp is splendid ceremonial show
taken as written
dour means stern and grim

explanation.surface: Showing off a harsh haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a style with the hair swept up high off the forehead, named after Madame de Pompadour.

clue.text: Wrongly interpret loyal support for girl defending prisoner

indicators.note: in a down clue a support goes underneath, so loyal is placed after the rest
defending means guarding on all sides, so the girl surrounds the prisoner

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
con is short for convict
true means faithful

explanation.surface: A faithful backer for a girl who stands up for a convict.
explanation.walkthrough: MIS-CON-S is the girl holding the prisoner, with TRUE placed beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: To misconstrue is to misunderstand or take the meaning of something incorrectly.

clue.text: Mediator ordered others to invest foreign currency

indicators.note: to invest is to surround or besiege, so the rearranged letters wrap round the money
ordered means put into a fresh sequence, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
the rouble is Russia's currency

explanation.surface: A go-between instructs others to put money into a foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Invest looks financial alongside currency, but it means surround, as an army invests a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A troubleshooter is brought in to settle disputes or fix problems, acting as a mediator between parties.

clue.text: Row over a poem about this beverage

indicators.note: about means around, so the poem goes on either side of the rest

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the next

parts.note: a range is a line or row, as of mountains
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quarrel over some verse written about this drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Row looks like a quarrel, but it is a line. O-RANGE-A-DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a sweet fizzy drink flavoured with oranges, so it is a beverage.

clue.text: Disorderly rush to take off in emergency

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a frantic, chaotic dash or struggle
second meaning: for fighter pilots to get airborne at once

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning comes from RAF fighter pilots ordered into the air at short notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hurried, disorderly struggle and an urgent launch of military aircraft.

clue.text: Meeting a collaborator according to custom

parts.note: a convention is a formal assembly
an ally works with you

explanation.surface: Meeting a partner in the traditional way.
explanation.walkthrough: Convention can also mean custom, which tempts the solver to hunt for a definition at the start; here it only supplies the meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventionally means in the usual accepted way, following established practice or tradition.

clue.text: Contracts for new weapons

parts.note: N abbreviates new
arrows are fired from bows

explanation.surface: Deals signed for a fresh supply of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: Contracts looks like a noun for agreements, but it is the verb, meaning shrinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrows as a verb means becomes smaller or tighter, just as contracts does.

clue.text: Reduce weight and become brighter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: make a load less heavy
second meaning: grow less dark, like the sky at dawn

explanation.walkthrough: One verb comes from light as opposed to heavy, the other from light as opposed to dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both easing a load so it is less heavy and growing paler or more illuminated.

clue.text: More than one place on a Russian river

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
the Ural is a river in Russia

explanation.surface: Several locations along a river in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' lets the first piece sit above the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural, in grammar, is the form of a word denoting more than one thing.

clue.text: Publicize divisions, say — they bring us to a standstill

definitions.text: they bring us to a standstill

parts.note: to air views is to make them public

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, so its sound matters rather than its spelling

parts.note: breaks are divisions or splits

explanation.surface: Announcing splits, which halts proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: Air brakes use compressed air to stop heavy vehicles such as lorries and trains, halting their passengers.

clue.text: A verse to honour Hymen discovered here

indicators.note: discovered means found lying uncovered, so the letters are already in the words beside it

parts.note: letters running across honour and Hymen

explanation.surface: A poem written in praise of Hymen, the Greek god of marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span the end of honour and most of Hymen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyme can mean a short poem or verse, as in a nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Russian writer's energetic student

parts.note: go-go means lively and dynamic
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A Russian author's lively pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was the nineteenth-century Russian novelist who wrote Dead Souls and The Overcoat.

clue.text: Express disapproval by giving the bird

parts.note: to boo is to jeer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Showing displeasure by jeering at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving the bird' is a British idiom for booing, so the whole clue reads as one phrase; in fact the bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby is a large tropical seabird related to the gannet.

clue.text: Male supporter accommodating Essex opener from now on

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so one piece is lodged within another

parts.note: a rafter holds up a roof

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so only the initial letter of the county is used

parts.note: first letter of the county

explanation.surface: A man's backer takes in the first batsman from Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is an English county with a cricket team, so its opener sounds like a batsman; here it is just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereafter means in future, from this time forward.

clue.text: Foul-sounding woman at this party?

parts.note: setter's reading: the word for a bird that sounds like foul, which is fowl
setter's reading: the woman whose name gives a women-only party before a wedding

explanation.walkthrough: Foul sounds like fowl, a farmyard bird, and the same word is British slang for a woman and names a bride's pre-wedding party.
explanation.definitionFit: Hen is informal for a woman, as in a hen party, the British bachelorette celebration.

clue.text: Oriental island needs a name

parts.note: Easter Island, in the Pacific
N abbreviates name

explanation.surface: An Asian island wants a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern both describe things from Asia or the East.

clue.text: Immortal birdman accompanying 26

parts.note: the answer to 26 abbreviates to E, as on a compass
a seabird, the tern, followed by a man's short name, Al

explanation.surface: A deathless bird-man travels alongside the previous answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birdman' must be split into bird and man; 26 is EASTERN, abbreviated to E as on a compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting for ever, without death or end, as an immortal being does.
